    //==
    // # Segment -> line / ray conversions
    //
    // The infinite carriers of an edge: the supporting line through A and B, and the
    // ray from A through B. Both need the unit direction A -> B, so both are
    // undefined for a degenerate (A == B) segment.

    // The infinite line through A and B, directed A -> B.
    SupportingLine(s: Line3D): InfiniteLine3D
        => (s.A, Direction3D(s.A.Between(s.B).Normalize));

    // The ray from A through B, directed A -> B.
    SupportingRay(s: Line3D): Ray3D
        => (s.A, Direction3D(s.A.Between(s.B).Normalize));

    // The infinite line through A and B, directed A -> B.
    SupportingLine(s: Line2D): InfiniteLine2D
        => (s.A, Direction2D(s.A.Between(s.B).Normalize));

    // The ray from A through B, directed A -> B.
    SupportingRay(s: Line2D): Ray2D
        => (s.A, Direction2D(s.A.Between(s.B).Normalize));

    //==
    // # Closest points between two flats
    //
    // The shortest connecting segment, returned A-on-first, B-on-second; its length
    // is the distance between the flats and its endpoints coincide when they cross.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skew_lines#Distance

    // The mutually nearest points of two infinite lines. For PARALLEL lines the
    // connector is anchored at the first line's origin (any common perpendicular has
    // the same length). Directions are unit, so the 2x2 normal system reduces to
    // denom = 1 - Dot(d1, d2)^2.
    ClosestPoints(a: InfiniteLine3D, b: InfiniteLine3D): Line3D
    {
        var d1 = a.Direction.Vector;
        var d2 = b.Direction.Vector;
        var r = b.Origin.Between(a.Origin);
        var f = d1.Dot(d2);
        var c = d1.Dot(r);
        var e = d2.Dot(r);
        var denom = 1.0 - f * f;
        var s = denom == 0.0 ? 0.0 : (f * e - c) / denom;
        var t = denom == 0.0 ? e : (e - f * c) / denom;
        return (a.Origin + d1 * s, b.Origin + d2 * t);
    }

    // The mutually nearest points of two segments, each parameter clamped to its own
    // [0, 1] extent (Ericson's segment-segment routine). Robust to a degenerate
    // (A == B) segment on either side: its span drops out of the division.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distance_between_two_lines
    ClosestPoints(sa: Line3D, sb: Line3D): Line3D
    {
        var d1 = sa.A.Between(sa.B);
        var d2 = sb.A.Between(sb.B);
        var r = sb.A.Between(sa.A);
        var a = d1.MagnitudeSquared;
        var e = d2.MagnitudeSquared;
        var f = d2.Dot(r);
        var c = d1.Dot(r);
        var b = d1.Dot(d2);
        var denom = a * e - b * b;
        var s0 = denom == 0.0 ? 0.0 : ((b * f - c * e) / denom).Clamp(0.0, 1.0);
        var t = (e == 0.0 ? 0.0 : (b * s0 + f) / e).Clamp(0.0, 1.0);
        var s = (a == 0.0 ? s0 : (t * b - c) / a).Clamp(0.0, 1.0);
        return (sa.A + d1 * s, sb.A + d2 * t);
    }

    //==
    // # Plane, half-space, and slab operations
    //
    // The signed-distance, side, intersection, containment and nearest-point bodies for
    // the types declared in `lines.types.plato`.
    //
    // Conventions:
    //   * `Contains` on the half-plane, half-space and slab regions is CLOSED: a point
    //     exactly on the bounding line/plane is contained, matching the interface doc
    //     ("for closed shapes the boundary counts as inside") and the `<=` in each
    //     declaration's own doc comment.
    //   * `ClosestPoint` on a REGION (half-plane, half-space) returns the query point
    //     itself when the query is inside, as `INearestPoint2D`/`3D` permits.
    //   * The signed distance of a point p from the world origin along a unit normal n
    //     is Dot(n, p) — written `p.PositionVector.Dot(n.Vector)` here, since a point
    //     is not a vector in this vocabulary (`transforms.library.plato`).

    //==
    // # Planes and half-spaces
    //
    // Hesse normal form: the plane is the set of p with Dot(Normal, p) = Distance,
    // so SignedDistance(p) = Dot(Normal, p) - Distance is the signed distance from
    // the plane, positive on the side the normal points to.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hesse_normal_form

    // The signed distance from `point` to the plane, positive on the side the
    // normal points to. Exact because Normal is a unit vector by its invariant.
    SignedDistance(pl: Plane, point: Point3D): Number
        => point.PositionVector.Dot(pl.Normal.Vector) - pl.Distance;

    // The signed distance from `point` to the half-plane's boundary line, positive
    // outside the half-plane.
    SignedDistance(h: HalfPlane2D, point: Point2D): Number
        => point.PositionVector.Dot(h.Normal.Vector) - h.Distance;

    // The foot of the perpendicular from `point` onto the plane.
    ClosestPoint(pl: Plane, point: Point3D): Point3D
        => point - pl.Normal.Vector * pl.SignedDistance(point);

    // Which side of the plane `point` lies on: +1 on the side Normal points to,
    // -1 behind, 0 on the plane. The sign of SignedDistance; the name every
    // clipping / BSP lesson reaches for.
    Side(pl: Plane, point: Point3D): Integer
        => pl.SignedDistance(point).Sign;

    // The plane through `point` with unit `normal`, in Hesse form: Distance is
    // Dot(normal, point), the signed distance from the world origin. The usual way
    // to build a plane from a point-and-normal (e.g. a triangle's vertex and face
    // normal).
    FromPointNormal(point: Point3D, normal: Direction3D): Plane
        => (normal, point.PositionVector.Dot(normal.Vector));

    // The same plane facing the other way: both Normal and Distance negated, so the
    // point set Dot(Normal, p) = Distance is unchanged while its front side flips.
    // The teachable one-liner that keeps the two fields in step.
    Flip(pl: Plane): Plane
        => (Direction3D(pl.Normal.Vector * -1.0), -pl.Distance);

    // The complementary closed half-space: the region on the other side of the same
    // boundary plane, obtained by flipping that plane.
    Flip(h: HalfSpace): HalfSpace
        => HalfSpace(h.Boundary.Flip);

    // Where the infinite line crosses the plane. Misses (Hit false) only when the
    // line is parallel to the plane (Dot(Normal, Direction) = 0), including a line
    // lying in the plane -- there is then no single crossing point.
    Intersect(l: InfiniteLine3D, pl: Plane): PlaneHit3D
    {
        var denom = l.Direction.Vector.Dot(pl.Normal.Vector);
        var t = 0.0 - pl.SignedDistance(l.Origin) / denom;
        return denom == 0.0
            ? (false, l.Origin, 0.0)
            : (true, l.PointAt(t), t);
    }

    // Where the ray crosses the plane. Misses when the ray is parallel to the plane
    // OR crosses behind the origin (t < 0).
    Intersect(r: Ray3D, pl: Plane): PlaneHit3D
    {
        var denom = r.Direction.Vector.Dot(pl.Normal.Vector);
        var t = 0.0 - pl.SignedDistance(r.Origin) / denom;
        return denom == 0.0 || t < 0.0
            ? (false, r.Origin, 0.0)
            : (true, r.PointAt(t), t);
    }
